bottleneck: Autism is not one condition but hundreds of genetic and developmental pathways converging on overlapping behavioral traits. This heterogeneity defeats one-size-fits-all research: findings in one subgroup do not replicate in another, clinical trials enroll mixed populations guaranteed to dilute any signal, and no biomarker stratifies patients for targeted intervention. The search for a unified theory of autism may itself be the error, yet funding and diagnostic systems still assume one entity.
current_state: Genetic testing identifies a cause in a minority of cases. Interventions remain behavioral; biology-guided treatments do not exist, and stratification research is only beginning.
title: Autism heterogeneity defeats unified models
why_it_blocks: Treating 'autism' as one entity guarantees failed trials. Stratification into biological subtypes is the precondition for any targeted therapy — and the field is only starting to build it.
